I'd say this game has the potential. But I wish there was a meh option on steam. This game has a decent gameplay loop that really feels like a bit of Ultrakill and Binding of Isaac melded together. The visuals and music work perfectly together for the atmosphere (Even if you're locked in to not getting murdered.) But this game is not without it's flaws. As it is right now, there's not much variety to each run. It boils down to Pick 2 guns + 2 gadgets, then go through the same levels with little to spice up each run. There's no way to affect the items you get each run (i.e. the 3D printers and scrappers from risk of rain.) and there's not really alternating challenge variants that appear that aren't spawn tons of crawlers, or collecting flowers (yes, and the temple run one,) and the only sort of progression in this game is play game, get tokens, unlock stuff in arcade, get new gadgets and, repeat. I'd prefer if there was say, This game is in early access so I know this game will get a lot of new things in the future. But right now, there's not much but a nice fast-paced gameplay loop.

阈限空间与老派竞技场FPS场景确实有不少类似之处，能抓住共同特点并把二者以极高的完成度融合到一起，oddcore应该算是第一位了！游戏整体也延续了《Ultrakill》等游戏飞天入地高机动的爽感，倒计时系统的设计让游戏流程更为紧凑，爽点比较集中，关卡包括跑酷、守点、收集、摧毁目标等几种形式，也会有一些小探秘或者跑酷奖励关卡，每一关的地图或者形式均有不同，还会包括各种随机事件，很好削弱了长线进程中场景重复带来的疲劳感。还有就是游戏的道具枪械解锁也是蛮有趣的，需要你用结算后的代币去游戏厅里玩各种游戏机获得票券来解锁，算是小小的增添了一些游戏性。 不过，在玩之前也有些注意事项——那就是jumpscare元素。 这玩意完全没法规避，跑酷跟随机事件里都会有，而且每一关卡结束后会出现名为watcher的生物，只要你离他过近或者开枪打它，这玩意立马就爬过来给你贴脸，大部分情况下都是可以躲掉的，但是关卡结束的时候它可能会刷新在你脸上，或者就躲在奖励后面，直接就给你抓了，切关都反应不过来，爽着爽着给你这么来一下也挺恶心的

竞技场射击+肉鸽+后室（阈限空间）题材居然可以碰撞出如此令人感到惊喜的火花，很不错。 将部分别的竞技场射击的射击续命换了一个形式加入游戏里，保证玩家在物品构筑外还有一层不确定因素可以反复挑战反复玩，天才般的想法。场景有很多阈限空间元素，再加上部分过渡层有经典神秘小房间更令人心满意足。游戏局外设计不只是枯燥单纯的换更多武器、更多技能，而是加入了街机厅，你可以在街机厅玩小游戏获取奖券换武器、技能和小宠物（可惜不能带进局内:( )初见会感到这是个很不错的想法，到后期能解锁的东西都解锁完了还能跑去街机厅玩点小游戏解解腻。游戏的机动性依赖于技能选择，选的好直接贴地飞行选不好就走地了，可以根据不同武器自由搭配合适你的技能。

Okay I'm sorry but am I the only one who thinks this game is way too dang difficult? Like I have been playing this game for quite a while now and I just can't for the life of me figure out how to deal with these high health damaging enemies. And that's not even mentioning the fact that this game throws a whole bunch of them at you all at once. Like I have tried time & time again, always upgrading my damage when I can and these enemies are just always freaking bullet sponges. Heck, even the eyes take multiple shots to take down. Freaking eyes that used to be 1 hit. And on top of that, some of these enemies are just blatantly overpowered. Like the hand that makes a whole bunch of enemies be immune to damage, the pyro that moves randomly extremely fast and can shoot fireballs at you, the telecrawl that can teleport behind you and could get a free hit on you like what the heck are these enemies? Also, another thing I don't like about this game is how the only good weapon is the pistol. Everything else is just freaking awful. SMG is extremely inaccurate and has a small clip. Shotgun only has 2 shells and has random bullet spread. The bat is so terrible that you need the slowmo gadget in order to properly use its alt-fire. But even then who the heck wants to stand still? Like seriously, these other weapons are so awful that you're just better off with only using the pistol. Especially considering that... not only does this game create the chance for your treasure chest to give you a weapon mod for your 2nd weapon that you hardly ever use, but you can only add 1 element to 1 weapon at a time and with how expensive it is to even do that, how crazy the tax can get, and how you always have to spend souls to get back to the hub and then spend more souls to increase the time, the luck to have 2 elemental weapons is extremely low. Also, speaking about the hub... why are there better versions of certain cards in the slot machine? Like for example, there's a red card that increases your damage by 2% but apparently, there's a better version of it that increases your damage by 5%. And the same thing goes for everything else. Green card that increases your health by 2, better version of it increases it by 3. Red card that increases your crit chance by 0.25%, better version of it increases it by 0.5% like why couldn't we have just keep it simple? The slot machine has enough luck already so why add even more luck? I didn't even know this was a thing before, I only found out 'cause I was paying attention to it while focusing on increasing my crit chance (due to how these enemies have an insane amount of health). But because of that, I now have to pay attention to which card I get which wastes more of my time on the oddcore like what the fudge devs? Also, more on the hub, I really don't like how the devs implemented the starting item roll in the diner like... I understand y'all don't want everyone to just pick any relic from the jump but why did y'all had to go to the lowest of the low and only allow us to roll 1 relic at a time while we have to wait a few seconds before rolling again? Like y'all might as well just let us pick whatever relic we want 'cause this game has a whole bunch already, it's hard enough already, and we can also roll hundreds of times before getting an epic or an odd so just let us pick whatever we want. Either that or y'all let us roll 4 at a time instead of just freaking 1. Also, speaking about the diner, the devs apparently worship 67 'cause 2 of the mixtapes contains one of the numbers. Like 1 mixtape has the number 6 on the right side of it and then the next mixtape has the number 7 on the left side of it. Heck, one of the songs is even called web667 like what the heck are we doing? Worshipping a number that was popularized by some guy who follows a demonic religion is one thing, but why the heck do we have to permanently acknowledge it in a videogame? But yeah all in all, I really can't recommend this. I tried to enjoy it but with how these enemies become absolute bullet sponges and how each of them can deal crazy damage to you later in a run, it seems like the only way to beat this game is if you get kidnapped by the watcher, get the "perma 1 hp, 1 shot everything" corruption, get multiple golden credit cards, and a whole bunch of blue cards in order to upgrade your push gadget so much that it has crazy range. Whether you do that or some other strategy, you have to get extremely lucky to beat this game 'cause if these enemies have so much health on variant 25 and you need to get to variant 50 in order to beat the game, may God help you. P.S. This game makes my PC make a hissing sound whenever I launch it up for some reason. P.P.S. Teddy bear is the only good offensive gadget if you're playing casually. Especially since you have the chance to come across the mod that makes it last a bit longer and makes enemies go after it no matter what. P.P.P.S. Only good arcade games are Rugpull 3000 and Hot Hoop. Everything else is freaking garbage. P.P.P.P.S. I also don't like how you have to go into the tutorial and then back into the main menu in order to unequip your weapons. It's very annoying.

This game is fundamentally streamer bait. Know that before you choose to play it. I have about 70mins play time in this game: 5min for tutorial, 5min for the first run where i couldn't figure out how to buy more time, 60+min for the second run once i figure that out. There is nothing interesting or challenging in the difficulty of this game, apparently you are supposed to have two weapons---i had only one in my 60min run. Apparently the thing on the left also does damage, apparently there are two combat move options---none of this mattered. The basic loop is trivial, the enemy variety is lacking, and the only thing you need to do to win is: run backwards, shoot, jump. If you're feeling spicy, dash out of boss attacks, or just tank them, because you'll have massive HP reserves anyway. Eventually i allowed my run to end, because it was clear that although the game was taking step functions in enemy health and damage, nothing about the loop was going to change. At the end of my second run, just about everything that wasn't tied to the arcade was unlocked. It's difficult to believe there'll be any meaningful meta progression. Finally, despite being advertised as a game based around 5min runs, this is definitely not true. These runs drag on for as long as your patience lasts, and the content, rooms, enemies, music, is recycled over and over.

I don't review games as much as I really should, but I felt compelled to here. I think that the devs have something good on their hands, but for a shooter of this kind it's severely lacking in game feel. A lot of the weapons lack strong sound design and (though I don't have much time racked up) have zero recoil. Player movement also feels pretty sluggish for what is on paper such a fast game. The game conceptually should be a blast but ends up feeling dull and like it's missing that "special sauce" that makes me want to keep coming back. For now, this will stand as a negative review, but what this game could be keeps me hopeful.

This game has a lot of interesting visuals and is a nice spin on what is otherwise a severely oversaturated aesthetic (the backrooms), but it really likes sauce, and there's a few mechanics about it that just plain annoy me. [hr][/hr] [h3]Weapons and Gadgets[/h3] The guns lack any kind of impact, and sound really weird. Many of them have sounds that are just kind of grating, though the frog is kinda funny. There isn't really enough information on them when looking at them, like I've never really been able to figure out what the shotgun's alt fire is supposed to do. Engineer, SMG, and the Fan are trash weapons that I don't know how you're supposed to do anything with. What bothers me the most about the guns though, specifically the SMG, Nailgun and Shotgun, is the absolutely abysmal mag size. Maybe it's some kind of weird autism on my part, but reloading every 2 seconds really gets on my nerves. There's no reason why the shotgun should only have 2 shots, it's barely worth the take anyways in terms of DPS. It feels like most of the weapons are just joke weapons save for a few that actually make any kind of difference. Gadgets are a little esoteric to me. Why is there a slide *and* a dash gadget? I figure in most games you can do these things without the need for crowding your mental stack by making deliberate choices as to which one you want. Taking anything that isn't dash and either grapple or slide just kinda feels like trolling yourself. I would think the best use of something called a "Gadget" would be something to supplement your build and weapons, rather than an extension of your movement or some esoteric mechanic interaction. The teddy bear is a fantastic example of a gadget, but as I said taking it would feel like crippling my movement. [h3]Card System[/h3] Speaking of esoteric, the card system is very poorly explained in my opinion, and after 5 hours I still don't think I'm building or making use of them right. From what I understand, taking a card with stats on it gives you those stats permanently? Then you can spend the cards you got them from? I can't really be sure because I don't really notice my stat increases, which I feel like stems from both the aforementioned lack of sauce and the visual clutter, the UI is really hard to decipher. Hitting Tab opens your stats page but I can't really tell where I'm at or what changed at a glance. Also, 10 cards for an elemental affinity seems pretty steep when I can barely find the time and opportunity to portal out and farm cards. If I do it too often, I get taxed, and some amount of souls always has to go to time. Even *when* I can afford an elemental affinity, I don't know what the hell they do because the game does not tell you what they do. If it does, then I've either completely missed it or it is hidden somewhere. I can obviously make an educated guess as to what they do, but at least some kind of tooltip would be very nice. [h3]Other Thoughts[/h3] Bosses are absurdly tanky, and I cannot understand how the Mole boss ever made it out of playtesting. It is the most frustrating boss to fight because it is just an endurance trial, a slog that is designed to waste your time and DPS check you in the most irritating way possible. The crawler hordes aren't even an issue, it's just that it pops out for literally seconds at a time in random places, with a seemingly a random amount of time between each emergence. [b]Very often[/b] it will pop out right under me, ensuring I take unavoidable damage unless I just so happened to be in the air. (The thought above ties into why I think the weapons are so lackluster, I feel like I do absolutely no damage despite building into damage and crits) In all my playtime I have never once fired a soul at my feet in front of a crate to heal myself. It is probably the most absurdly tacked on mechanic I can think of. Just make it so that crates always heal you by a little or remove the feature. It's not worth using souls to do anything but add time and get cards. The arcade is also pretty neat and has a nice vibe, but aside from weapons and gadgets, everything else is just ticket burning. After you get the weapons and gadgets, it's basically a non-feature. Some permanent buffs or something for large amounts of tickets would be nice. [hr][/hr] All in all, I think it has a lot of good potential, as I said. It is my hope when I leave reviews that I will help games get better and improve with time. I know it's an Early Access game, and I feel like reviews that aren't one sentence memes or "it's trash" trolling are valuable to a game like this, I want to see it succeed more because there is a genuinely great game here. [b]As it stands, I cannot recommend the game[/b], because recommending it in its current state is mostly just to encourage others to engage with the aesthetics, which is risk for something so saturated, for the music, or just for the love of supporting indies, which if you're going to do anyway, I can't fault you for. This is all my opinion, so feel free to take it or leave it with as many grains of salt as you like. However, I would really like to enjoy this game more, these petty nitpicks really add up and hold me back from enjoying it as much as other games in the genre.

It ain't it, the game is quite dull to be honest. The enviroments, despite being all kooky and zany are just regular boring arenas, by the way some of them look I expected walking on walls and other crazy stuff but nah, it's all just fluff. Enemies aren't very interesting either, there is little variety and they mostly just run at you, they aren't very ODD. Bosses are bullet sponges and feel like a chore. Weapons have way too small magazines and too long cooldowns, they aren't satisfying to use. Upgrades are mostly just stat increases, probably the biggest letdown in a roguelite. Movement feels very sluggish when your dashes and whatnots are on cooldown. Music? If you don't collect additional hidden tracks you will be listening to the same stuff over and over again. Graphics are lovely, but that's my personal preference for this style. As for minor gripes the stat window has no descriptions for icons so you don't really know what is what. OVERALL, I suggest waiting for 1.0, but I doubt it's gonna change much.

Oddcore is the kind of game that throws you into absolute madness and somehow makes every second of it amazing. The world is bizarre, the atmosphere is unforgettable, and you’re constantly wondering what insanity is waiting around the next corner. The best part? It lets you become ridiculously powerful. Every upgrade feels meaningful, stacking new abilities until you’re tearing through enemies like the nightmare belongs to you. Experimenting with different upgrades is half the fun, and the payoff is incredibly satisfying. Weird, unforgettable, and an absolute blast from start to finish.
one of the most fun, interesting and addictive shooters i have played in a long time.

I initially loved ODDCORE's aesthetic, then briefly wrote it off as a lazy attempt to cash in on the trending "liminal space/anomaly" hype, but I eventually locked in and stopped overthinking and started appreciating the game for what it is. It's got smooth movement, great power scaling, high run variety, and unique enemies. The whole "countdown to purge" mechanic adds a brilliant sense of urgency that I wouldn't normally get in any other roguelike shooter. I sometimes stream it for my friends, and they can't process what's happening. TLDR: Definitely takes a little getting used to, but I highly recommend it.

I love the vibes of the game. The atmosphere really captures that dreamcore aesthetic and the immediate gameplay loop of needing to outrun the clock makes it so that every moment feels frantic, even with the timer actually being fairly generous. There's plenty of weapons to experiment with and more content is still being added. My only complaints are that needing to convert needing tokens into tickets can be a bit of a slog (my tip is to play ski ball early on and then the coin pusher once you have an excess of tokens) and certain enemies can kill the pacing at times. I'm not the biggest fan of roguelikes nor arena shooters so I don't see myself playing this for hundreds for hours, but I feel I still got my money's worth. Overall, 6/10
